title: flows.drafts.propose payload
description: A DRAFT automation for the owner to review. It is not an automation yet: it does not run, it holds no permissions, and it never will until a person opens it, fills the gaps and turns it on. Write the skeleton you are sure about and put everything you had to guess in `notes` — a guess the owner can see is useful, a guess hidden inside a parameter is not. This mirrors `hub/schemas/flow.schema.json`, the contract the hub enforces on save; the hub is the authority and it refuses anything that does not match.

name.description: What the owner will read in their list of automations, in THEIR language and in their words — «Avisar cuando no venga alguien a su cita», not «no_show handler».

notes.description: What you could NOT work out, one short sentence each, in the owner's language: an amount you invented, a name you were not sure of, something they asked for that this format cannot express. Send an empty list only when there is genuinely nothing to check.

definition.description: The automation document. It is LINEAR: the steps run in order, and a condition that does not pass ENDS the run — there is no branch, no loop and no «else».

triggers.description: What starts it. Exactly one, or none to mean «only by hand».

kind.description: `event`: something happened in the business. `cron`: on a clock. `at`: once, at an instant. `manual`: only when somebody presses run.

event.description: Only with `kind: event` — the name of the thing that happens, exactly as the module that owns it emits it. Use one you know this hub really has; if you are not sure of the name, say so in `notes` rather than inventing one. Common ones: `sale.completed`, `customer.created`, `appointments.appointment.created`, `appointments.appointment.no_show`, `appointments.appointment.cancelled`, `online_booking.booking.created`, `reservations.reservation.created`, `inventory.stock_changed`, `tables.session.closed`, `cash_register.session_closed`, `whatsapp_inbox.message.received`.

filter.description: Only with `kind: event` — narrow which occurrences start it, same shape as a condition's `when` but with `event.<field>` paths.

cron.description: Only with `kind: cron` — five fields `min hour dom mon dow`, read in the shop's own timezone. `0 9 * * *` is every day at 09:00.

at.description: Only with `kind: at` — an RFC-3339 instant WITH its offset, e.g. `2026-09-01T09:00:00+02:00`.

steps.description: What it does, IN ORDER. Keep it short: most useful automations are one trigger and one action.

id.description: How later steps refer to this one (`steps.<id>.<field>`). Unique within the automation.

kind.description: Only these three. The hub also runs `http`, `ai` and `notify` steps and the owner can add them by hand, but you may not propose one: an `http` calls a URL nobody chose, a `notify` costs money for every message sent, and an `ai` is another billed call. If what they asked for needs one, propose the closest thing you CAN express and say what is missing in `notes`.

command.description: Only with `kind: command` — the action to run, by its full name (`tasks.tasks.create`, `customers.notes.add`). Use one of the tools you were given for this hub: a name that does not exist here is refused when the owner saves.

params.description: Only with `kind: command` — what the action receives. A value is either something you write literally, a PATH that copies a field of the run (`input.customer_id` — this keeps its type), or a sentence with `{{input.name}}` placeholders inside it (this is always text). `input` is what the trigger carried.

when.description: Only with `kind: condition` — a guard. Every comparison must hold or the run STOPS HERE, quietly and successfully. Money is in cents: 100,00 € is 10000.

seconds.description: Only with `kind: delay` — how long to wait FROM NOW. There is no way to wait until a date carried in the payload; if that is what they asked for, say so in `notes`.

comparison.description: One field, compared. `{"input.total": {"gte": 10000}}`. A field that is not there never matches, except with `exists: false`.
